result:
Fixed `scenario.json` per the reader findings.

What the reader got right and what changed:
- Ambiguous attachment: "whose description mentions offline sync" could modify the issue. Rewrote as "the private team with MOB in its key that is described as owning offline sync" — the relative clause can only modify the team (a key can't be "described as owning" something), so the issue-description reading is gone.
- Unnatural stacking: dropped the issue-title identifier entirely. Each team now holds exactly one issue, so the request just says "the issue on the ... team" — one fewer stacked filter, and the title is no longer a condition. Added condition c1 ("the issue on the team", `R:Issue.teamId`, now on the query edge) so the link is still explicit in the reference.

Kept by judgment:
- The team is still pinned by key substring ("with MOB in its key") plus private flag plus described-as phrase rather than by name. Naming the team ("Mobile") would make the description and privacy filters untestable: team keys are unique, so description/visibility decoys must be different teams that still satisfy the key phrase — only a substring-style key phrase allows each decoy to fail exactly one condition. The seed's lookalike teams (MOB, MOBX, MOBP, MOB Support) give the careful user a realistic reason to disambiguate this way.
- The F1 description decoy (team named "Offline Sync Lab" whose description covers prototypes) stays: with "described as" wording it unambiguously fails, and it remains the tempting near miss for solvers that match the phrase against the name.

Decoys unchanged in structure (witnesses `i-sup-1`, `i-and-1` for key F1/F0; `i-mobx-1` for description F1; `i-mobp-1` for private F0), background WEB team still fails all three team conditions.
